newsitem.title: USA: California nurses strike Kaiser Permanente hospitals.
newsitem.headline: California nurses strike Kaiser Permanente hospitals.

text.p: Thousands of nurses employed by the nation's largest health maintenance organisation, Kaiser Permanente, walked off the job Thursday to protest a breakdown in contract negotiations, their union said.

The strike, which will continue Friday, involves 7,500 nurses at 47 northern California hospitals and clinics. Striking nurses were joined by some other health care workers, housekeepers and clerical workers represented by other unions.
"We're picketing everywhere," said Charles Idelson, spokesman for the California Nurses Association, which is staging the strike. "It's been very effective."
Kaiser said all of its facilities remained open despite the strike, but at reduced service levels. Its emergency rooms were fully staffed.
Kaiser re-scheduled elective surgeries and patient appointments, but said its 3,500 physicians, with the help of nurse managers flown in from southern California, were filling in for the strikers.

The nurses are fighting proposed wage reductions, reduced staffing levels and deep reductions in their own health care benefits. The California Nurses Association said Kaiser has tried to displace some of its most experienced nurses with lower-paid, less-experienced employees.
The association said these patterns have caused the quality of care in Kaiser hospitals to decline, resulting in long waits for emergency care and a shortage of specialised nurses on hand.
The association staged a similar one-day strike in April, and last year authored a ballot initiative imposing strict regulations on health maintenance organisations. Voters defeated that initiative.
